title: The writer is a plain Claude Code session, and scripts verify around it
description: Rewrites F2 of the cost/code/CI plan: the writer stops being a subagent with a brief and becomes the measured plain reference itself, and the plugin's verification moves out of the session into scripts the drive runs. Measured on this repository: the task text is 1 to 2 percent of an executor's opening context, no executor of 114 read the cache on its first request, and cache rebuilds after a five-minute pause were 26 to 38 percent of executor spend. The confirming run measures what this costs against plain at the same model and effort before any claim is written; its first stage runs after the clause-coverage task and its second stage is this phase's exit. Every task here lands before the phase that removes the old path, so the old path stays available as a rollback for one release. This phase also carries the two moves cancelled out of P130 (tests and development code leave the shipped plugin), the four medium faults scheduled to this release, and one task for the low findings carried from BF4 under D9.
desiredOutcome: Every task's writer runs as a headless top-level Claude Code session the drive launches on plain's own prompt, on a model pinned by full id at high effort, under a per-session budget, priced by the session's own total_cost_usd, and returning one JSON answer per acceptance clause. After the session the drive proves red-first through a throwaway git tree and locks the digest of the task's test files, checks clause coverage, and runs the task gate; a red gate or an uncovered clause resumes the same session for at most two rounds. A reviewer session that opened no file is not a review, and a phase-review finding blocks only after a second pass validates it, going back to the writer's session while its cache is warm.

findings.issue: Nothing in the drive's state tells a writer session that is still running from one that finished. WRITER_RULE says 'Run the run: line ... in Bash, in the background; then next.' A `next` taken straight after the background launch meets, for a first dispatch, executor None plus the dispatched-executor mark and asks no-executor-return (offering resume/retry while the session runs, so a second session can be started on the same tree); for a resume round it meets a filed executor with no gated mark and runs the task gate on the session's half-written tree, which can record a spurious red and spend a resume round. The record file (session_record) is the only completion signal and advance does not consult it before deciding. ws1-ws7 play each session synchronously (_play_session) before the next `next`, so no case can see this.
findings.resolution: Make completion explicit: either word the rule 'run it in the background and take `next` only when it exits', or (better, mechanical) have advance return a `wait` step while a writer session was dispatched for the current round and its record has not appeared (and no record means not finished), and add a case that calls `next` between dispatch and the run.

findings.issue: writer_test_command / writer_prove demand a red proof from every task that has a tests.add file, whatever its tests.mode (only the no-tests.add case consults the mode). The repo's rule is that red-first is owed by tdd (expectRedFirst is mode == tdd; the reviewer rule says not-attempted for gate-only and regression). A regression-mode writer task whose new test passes at HEAD gets no block from the helper, so it becomes red-refused-writer, two resume rounds are spent telling the session to make a passing test fail, then red-refused and a retry or block. A gate-only task that happens to name a test is treated the same way.

findings.issue: inert is computed as 'the mutated sweep had no red', not 'the mutation changed no verdict'. If the commit already holds a suite red unmutated, an inert mutation is reported as 'ran' with red N, so a mutation that did nothing reads as evidence. Not a false miss (the baseline check filters those), but the inert signal is lost exactly when the tree is not green.
findings.resolution: Compare against the unmutated sweep's red set (or treat reds that the baseline check later lists as baseline_red as not counting toward inert).

findings.issue: The scan is bounded per declared file (two git grep calls, a cap of 8 files, the total printed) but not per brief. dependant_lines passes every declared entry to _impact.dependants with no limit on how many files are searched or how many lines are rendered, and the section goes into three artifacts (executor brief, writer prompt, reviewer brief). Measured read-only on this repo with the declared files of the 184-file task P130.8: 8.8 s for one scan, 337 lines, about 121 KB of section text. Tasks with 504 and 235 files exist in this plan (P131.1, P131.2). The per-call 20 s timeout times two times N files has no ceiling either. Test im7 pins only the per-file figure, with three files, so nothing fails if the per-brief figure is unbounded. A large rename task would get a section that is slow to build and swamps the brief, which is the opposite of a bounded brief.
findings.resolution: Give dependants()/render() a per-brief budget: search at most K declared files (or stop at a wall-clock deadline), render at most M lines, and print 'N of M declared files searched / lines shown' so the cut is counted, not silent. Add an im7 case with more declared files than the budget that asserts the git-call count and the printed totals.

findings.issue: For a JS/TS file the dominant importer is invisible, and the brief then states it positively. Probed on a throwaway fixture: src/api.ts imported by src/main.ts as `import {fmt} from './api'` and src/util.js required as `require('./util')` - the importer is matched only when it spells the extension. src/api.ts rendered as 'c.json (path)' alone (main.ts missing). When nothing else names the file the section prints NONE_LINE, 'No tracked file names any of this task's files', which asserts a negative the scan cannot support. The docstring's WHAT IT CANNOT SEE admits the gap, but the brief the agent reads does not. The task asked for a language-agnostic helper; the Python module-name reading has no JS/TS counterpart, and im5 covers .js/.md/.json by path and basename only, no extensionless import.
findings.resolution: For JS/TS-family files (.js .mjs .cjs .jsx .ts .tsx) also search the extensionless stem and classify a line as an import when it is a quoted relative specifier ending in the stem (`from './api'`, `require('../x/api')`). Add a fixture case for it. Independently, soften NONE_LINE to 'No tracked file names ... by path, basename, or (Python) module name' so the one-line result states what was searched.

findings.issue: The private-name rule keeps a leading-underscore name when the file 'also references the module'. A document that mentions the module (PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, a research note) therefore counts for every private name of it: the probe lists `_norm in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md` for _impact.py and `_borrowed_wrapper_names in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md` for _deps.py. Names sorted fewest-files-first put these single-file noise hits ahead of real callers.
findings.resolution: Apply the private-name rule only to files whose reference kind is path or import, not basename, or only to code files.

tasks.title: One script runs a writer or a reviewer as a headless top-level session under a per-session budget and prints its cost from the session's own result
tasks.description: Add plugins/audit/scripts/governance/run-agent-session.py, an entry point that runs one role as a headless top-level Claude Code session in the task's tree: claude -p with --model given as a full model id (never an alias), --effort, --permission-mode auto, --output-format stream-json, --max-budget-usd from the caller, and --plugin-dir naming the running plugin so its hooks act on the session. The writer role passes no --agents or --agent and sends no agent body. The reviewer role passes --agents built from agents/audit-reviewer.md and --agent audit-reviewer. --resume <session id> continues a recorded session. The prompt goes on stdin, never in argv: a sibling session's pkill -f matches command lines. The session runs in its own process group with its own TMPDIR under the task's scratch, and its stream is saved under the state dir. It prints one line: the session id, the stream result's total_cost_usd, and the exit. A stream that ends with no result event is could-not-run naming the stream path. A new entry point owes a selftest in tests/, safe_stdio first in __main__, a layer in tools/lints/_deps.py LAYERS, a tree line and a section in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, and the PATH_PREAMBLE. Acceptance: (1) the writer argv carries the full model id, the effort, permission mode auto, the budget and the plugin dir, and neither --agents nor --agent; (2) the reviewer argv carries --agents built from audit-reviewer.md and --agent audit-reviewer; (3) on both roles the prompt arrives on stdin and is absent from argv; (4) the printed cost is the stream result's total_cost_usd and the printed id is the stream's session id; (5) a stream with no result event prints could-not-run naming the stream and exits non-zero; (6) --resume adds the recorded session id and changes nothing else in the argv; (7) the child runs in a process group of its own; (8) one live run's printed cost equals the transcript re-price (checked in the confirming run's first stage, not by the suite).
